'''Kristin Estella Lauter''' (born 1969)<ref>Birth year from [http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n2008017385.html Library of Congress catalog data], retrieved 2018-11-29.</ref> is an American mathematician and [[cryptographer]] whose research interest is broadly in application of [[number theory]] and [[algebraic geometry]] in cryptography. She is particularly known for her work in the area of [[elliptic curve cryptography]]. She was a researcher at [[Microsoft Research]] in [[Redmond, Washington]], from 1999–2021 and the head of the Cryptography Group from 2008–2021; her group  developed [[Microsoft SEAL]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kristin Lauter, Principal Researcher and Partner Research Manager|website=[[Microsoft]] |url=https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/people/klauter/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200707092547/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/people/klauter/|archive-date=7 July 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> In April 2021, Lauter joined [[Facebook]] AI Research (FAIR) as the West Coast Head of Research Science.<ref name=fair>{{cite web|title=Kristin E. Lauter|url=https://ai.facebook.com/people/kristin-lauter/|publisher=Facebook AI Research|access-date=7 May 2021}}</ref> She became the President-Elect of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in February 2014<ref name="awmelect">{{cite periodical |title=President-Elect: Kristin Lauter, Microsoft Research |periodical=Association for Women in Mathematics Newsletter |date=November–December 2013 |volume=43 |issue=6 |pages=4–6}}</ref> and served as President February 1, 2015 - January 31, 2017.

==Education and career==
Lauter received her [[Bachelor of Arts]], [[Master of Science]], and [[Ph.D.]], all in mathematics, from the [[University of Chicago]], in 1990, 1991, and 1996, respectively.

Prior to joining [[Microsoft]], she held positions as a visiting scholar at [[Max Planck Institut fur Mathematik]] in Bonn, Germany (1997), T.H. Hildebrandt research assistant professor at the University of Michigan (1996-1999), and a visiting researcher at Institut de Mathematiques Luminy in France (1999).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2016/06/KLCurriculum-Vitae2016.pdf|title= Kristin Lauter Curriculum Vitae|website= [[Microsoft]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190531014614/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2016/06/KLCurriculum-Vitae2016.pdf|archive-date=31 May 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=77976}}</ref>

In 1999, Lauter joined Microsoft to work on her research in [[cryptography]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/tales-from-the-cryptography-lab-with-dr-kristin-lauter/|title=Tales from the Crypt(ography) Lab with Dr. Kristin Lauter|date=2018-04-11|website=Microsoft Research|language=en-US|access-date=2019-07-17}}</ref>  She has worked on developing new cryptographic systems, research on [[Quantum computing|post quantum systems]], and researching to find faults in current cryptographic systems.

In 2005, she worked with coworkers at Microsoft to develop a cryptographic algorithm from supersingular isogeny graphs.  She created a HASH function from it and presented it at the [[NIST hash function competition]].<ref name=":0" />

Dr. Kristin Lauter is also known for her work in [[homomorphic encryption]], which has been commonly used in [[Machine learning|machine-learning]], building [[mathematical model]]s, [[Artificial intelligence|private AI]], and the collection of [[DNA|genomic data]].<ref name=":0" />  She has also worked on encryption with the [[Cloud computing|Cloud]]. She has given many tutorials on homomorphic encryption for broad audiences. A specific tutorial on homomorphic encryption allowed her to meet some iDASH organizers to whom she explained her encryption techniques, such as [[edit distance]] and [[Chi-squared test|chi-squared statistics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/site/awmmath/home/awm-2013-elections/kristin-lautner|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160530173115/https://sites.google.com/site/awmmath/home/awm-2013-elections/kristin-lautner|title=Kristin Lauter, Microsoft Research|publisher =Association for Women in Mathematics|archive-date=30 May 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Beginning in April 2021, Lauter joined Facebook AI Research as West Coast Head of Research Science,  leading the Seattle and Menlo Park Labs with groups in Core Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Robotics, Natural Language Processing, and other areas.<ref name=fair />

==Service==
She is a co-founder of the Women in Numbers Network,<ref>{{cite web|title=Women in Number Theory|url=http://womeninnumbertheory.org|website=Women in Number Theory|access-date=3 February 2017}}</ref> a research collaboration community for women in number theory.  The first conference was held in 2008 and it was called the WIN Conference.  Groups of number theorists work on research and have published about 50 papers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://womeninnumbertheory.org/|title=Women in Number Theory – A Mathematical Community|language=en-US|access-date=2019-07-17}}</ref>  She served on the Advisory Board<ref>{{cite web|title=Current Members of the Scientific Advisory Board|url=http://www.birs.ca/about/governance/scientific-management/scientific-advisory-board/current-members|website=Banff International Research Center|access-date=3 February 2017}}</ref> of the [[Banff International Research Station]] and on the Council<ref>{{cite web|title=Council of the AMS|url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/council/member-council|website=Council of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=3 February 2017}}</ref> of the [[American Mathematical Society]]. She served as president of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] 2015–2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/about/history/|title=History|website=Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM)|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-07}}</ref> From 2014 to 2016, Lauter served as a Council Member at Large for the American Mathematical Society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-27 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref> She currently is serving a second term on the board of trustees of the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] (MSRI); her terms on the MSRI Board run from 2018–2026.<ref name=msri>{{cite web|title=Board of Trustees|url=https://www.msri.org/web/msri/about-msri/governance-directory/board-of-trustees|publisher=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|access-date=14 April 2021}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Lauter and her coauthors were awarded the [[Algorithmic Number Theory Symposium#Selfridge Prize|Selfridge Prize]] at [[Algorithmic Number Theory Symposium#ANTS VIII (2008)|ANTS VIII]] for their paper ''Computing Hilbert Class Polynomials''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://math.ucalgary.ca/ants/ |title=Eighth Algorithmic Number Theory Symposium ANTS-VIII, May 17-22, 2008, Banff Centre, Banff, Alberta (Canada) |access-date=2012-07-13 |archive-date=2012-07-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120722191710/http://math.ucalgary.ca/ants/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>  She was elected to the 2015 Class of  Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to arithmetic geometry and cryptography as well as service to the community."<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref>

In 2017, she was selected as a fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in the inaugural class.<ref>{{cite web|title=2018 Inaugural Class of AWM Fellows|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2018-awm-fellows|website=awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|access-date=9 January 2021}}</ref>

She was chosen as the Pólya Lecturer for the [[Mathematical Association of America]], lasting from 2018–2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/Students-Education/Programs-Initiatives/Thinking-of-a-Career-in-Applied-Mathematics/Profiles/Detail/kristin-lauter-cryptography-research-managerprincipal-researcher|title=Kristin Lauter|website=SIAM|language=en-US|access-date=2019-07-17}}</ref><ref name="MAA Pólya Lectures">{{cite web | title=Pólya Lectures | website=Mathematical Association of America | url=https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/lecture-awards/p%C3%B3lya-lecturers | access-date=2022-11-27 | archive-date=2021-01-21 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121010210/https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/lecture-awards/p%C3%B3lya-lecturers | url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2020 she was elected a [[fellow]] of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) with the citation "Kristin E. Lauter, Microsoft Research, is being recognized for the development of practical cryptography and for leadership in the mathematical community."<ref name="siamfellow">{{cite web |title=SIAM Announces Class of 2020 Fellows |date=31 March 2020 |url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/siam-announces-class-of-2020-fellows |publisher=Society of Industrial and Applied Mathematics |access-date=31 March 2020}}</ref>

In 2020, she was elected Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], in the Section on Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Mathematics People - AAAS Fellows Elected|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202103/rnoti-p434.pdf|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=68|pages=437}}</ref>

In 2021, Lauter was elected as an honorary member of the Royal Spanish Mathematical Society. Real Sociedad Matemática Española (RSME), founded in 1911, is the oldest mathematical society of Spain.<ref>{{cite web|title=Figalli, Lauter, Teissier y Uhlenbeck, nuevos socios de honor de la RSME|date=12 February 2021 |url=https://www.rsme.es/2021/02/figalli-lauter-teissier-y-uhlenbeck-nuevos-socios-de-honor-de-la-rsme/|publisher=Real Sociedad Matemática Española|access-date=11 April 2021}}</ref>

In 2022 she was selected to be the SIAM Block Community Lecturer.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 SIAM Block Community Lecture Presented by Dr. Kristin Lauter |url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/2022-siam-block-community-lecture-presented-by-dr-kristin-lauter |access-date=2022-05-28 |website=SIAM News |date=10 March 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref>
